title: Tag 17 dead-end corridor behind the north-face chevrons detected in 2020 and later inspected with a camera
summary: Jeffrey tells of Tag 17 dead-end corridor behind the north-face chevrons detected in 2020 and later inspected with a camera, about 2020-recent at Egypt (no place named), and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.
place_text: North face of the Great Pyramid, Giza, Egypt

tellings.quote: They detected it. Yeah, they this was this was detected by the team in 2020 >> Okay. and they recently went inside of this with a microscopic camera.

plain: A researcher named Jeffrey told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in 2026 that a scan of the Great Pyramid in Egypt made in 2020, by a team that included a man named Filippo, picked up a dead-end corridor, labelled Tag 17, behind the large angled stone blocks on the pyramid's north face. He says that the corridor was recently looked at from inside with a tiny camera, which, if true, would show the scan can find hidden spaces inside the pyramid.
